map.summary: A comprehensive overview of the STM8L050J3 ultra-low-power 8-bit microcontroller and its datasheet. It describes the CPU, memory, clock system, low-power modes, reset and power supervision, RTC, DMA, ADC, timers, communication interfaces, comparators, GPIO and pin functions, SWIM debugging, and the serial bootloader. It also covers register and memory maps, interrupt vectors, option bytes, operating limits, current consumption, clock and voltage characteristics, peripheral timing and accuracy, ADC input and PCB design guidance, supply decoupling and EMC, the SO8N package, ordering information, revision history, and legal notices.
map.short_description: Summarizes the STM8L050J3 architecture, peripherals, programming and debugging features, electrical specifications, application guidance, and package and ordering details.

sections.title: STM8L050J3 datasheet overview and contents
sections.summary: The opening material identifies the STM8L050J3 as an ultra-low-power 8-bit MCU with 8 KB of Flash, 256 bytes of data EEPROM, 1 KB of RAM, and a range of integrated peripherals. It highlights operating voltage and temperature ranges, low-power modes and current figures, STM8 core performance, reset and clock management, RTC, DMA, ADC, timers, communication interfaces, comparators, I/O, and development support. The remainder is navigational: the contents outline chapters on device operation, pins, memory and registers, interrupts, option bytes, electrical and package characteristics, ordering, and revision history; the table and figure lists index the supporting specifications, measurements, diagrams, and package information.
sections.short_description: Introduces the STM8L050J3 microcontroller, summarizes its features, and lists the datasheet’s contents, tables, and figures.

sections.title: Overview of the STM8L050J3’s features, architecture, low-power operation, peripherals, and power management.
sections.summary: This section introduces the STM8L050J3 ultra-low-power 8-bit microcontroller, outlining its memory, voltage range, peripherals, CPU architecture, interrupt controller, low-power modes, and power-supply and reset arrangements. It also explains BOR and PVD voltage monitoring, regulator operating modes, and clock management, including clock sources, prescaling, safe switching, security, and clock output.
sections.short_description: Overview of the STM8L050J3’s architecture and features, including low-power operation, voltage monitoring, regulator modes, and clock management.

sections.title: Clock tree and oscillator sources
sections.summary: Shows how oscillator sources feed the system, RTC, beeper, and configurable clock output, with clock selection and prescaler controls. Notes that HSE and LSE may use crystals, ceramic resonators, or bypassed external clock sources.
sections.short_description: Presents the STM8L050J3 clock tree, its clock routing and prescalers, and notes on external clock source options.

sections.title: RTC, memories, programming guidance, and DMA
sections.summary: Summarizes the BCD real-time clock, alarms, and periodic wakeups; RAM, Flash, EEPROM, and option bytes; the risks of executing from empty program memory and SWIM connection constraints; and the four-channel DMA controller’s supported peripherals.
sections.short_description: Describes RTC calendar and wakeup functions, memory resources, precautions for programming devices with empty Flash, and DMA capabilities.

sections.title: Analog peripherals, system routing, and timers
sections.summary: Lists ADC1 conversion, scan, watchdog, and trigger features, along with two low-power comparators and their threshold options. Describes system configuration and routing functions and the general-purpose and basic timers, including their counters, prescalers, capture/compare, PWM, and interrupt capabilities.
sections.short_description: Covers ADC and comparator features, signal routing and remapping, and timer resources and capabilities.

sections.title: Watchdogs, beeper, and SPI
sections.summary: Describes the window watchdog’s role in detecting software faults and the independently clocked IWDG. Covers the beeper’s 1, 2, or 4 kHz output and SPI1’s synchronous transfer modes, 8 Mbit/s maximum speed, master/slave operation, CRC, and DMA support.
sections.short_description: Explains the watchdog timers and beeper output, then outlines SPI communication modes, speed, and features.

sections.title: I2C and USART interfaces
sections.summary: Details I2C multi-master operation, standard and fast speeds, addressing modes, SMBus and PMBus support, CRC, and DMA. Describes USART full-duplex asynchronous communication, baud-rate generation, SPI emulation, smartcard, IrDA, single-wire half-duplex, and DMA support.
sections.short_description: Summarizes I2C1 bus modes and protocol support alongside USART1 serial communication features.

sections.title: Infrared interface and development support
sections.summary: Describes timer output-compare channels for generating infrared remote-control signals and surveys development tools, including STice, STVD, STVP, starter kits, evaluation boards, and low-cost debugging/programming tools. It then introduces the SWIM single-wire interface, which supports non-intrusive real-time debugging and fast memory programming. For firmware that reuses the SWIM pin as GPIO, an initial delay of about five seconds helps preserve programming access; firmware may also re-enable SWIM under specified conditions, and the delay can be removed in final locked firmware.
sections.short_description: Covers infrared signal generation, development tools, and SWIM debugging and programming, including guidance for sharing the SWIM pin with GPIO.

sections.title: Bootloader
sections.summary: The STM8L050J3 includes a bootloader supporting USART on pins 8 and 1 (PC5 as TxD and PC6 as RxD). It downloads application software to RAM, program memory, and data memory through standard serial interfaces, complementing SWIM-based programming. The cited bootloader documentation is user manual UM0560.
sections.short_description: Describes the built-in serial bootloader and its role in downloading software to device memories.

sections.title: Pin description and system configuration
sections.summary: This section documents the STM8L050J3 SO8N pinout and the functions available on each pin, including GPIO, oscillator, USART, SPI, I2C, timer, ADC, comparator, RTC, SWIM, and BEEP functions. Tables define pin types, input and output characteristics, reset states, and abbreviations. Notes explain shared-pin interactions, alternate-function remapping, SWIM availability on pin 1, output configuration recommendations for unbonded GPIOs, and open-drain and slope-control details. System configuration options allow selected functions to be remapped through registers described in reference manual RM0031.
sections.short_description: Presents the SO8N pinout, pin-function and electrical-configuration tables, GPIO cautions, and remapping options.

sections.title: Memory and register map
sections.summary: The memory map identifies regions for RAM (up to 1 Kbyte, including the stack), data EEPROM (256 bytes), option bytes, GPIO and peripheral registers, boot ROM (2 Kbytes), CPU/SWIM/debug/interrupt-controller registers, reset and interrupt vectors, and low-density Flash program memory (8 Kbytes). The figure also locates hardware-register blocks for peripherals such as DMA, system configuration, clock, watchdogs, RTC, communication interfaces, timers, ADC, and routing interface. Accompanying notes direct readers to tables for memory boundaries, hardware registers, I/O port registers, and CPU/SWIM/debug controller registers; Table 5 begins the Flash and RAM boundary listing.
sections.short_description: Introduces the device memory map, its address regions and peripheral registers, and the boundary-address table.

sections.title: Memory ranges and I/O port registers
sections.summary: The memory map specifies 1 Kbyte of RAM at 0x00 0000–0x00 03FF and 8 Kbytes of flash program memory at 0x00 8000–0x00 9FFF. The I/O port register map covers ports A–D, listing each port’s output latch (ODR), input pin value (IDR), data direction (DDR), and control registers 1 and 2 (CR1/CR2), with their addresses and reset states.
sections.short_description: Lists the RAM and flash memory ranges and the I/O hardware register addresses, names, and reset values for ports A through D.

sections.title: Flash and DMA1 channel 0 registers
sections.summary: The register map notes the reserved area at 0x00 502E–0x00 5049, then lists flash control, program-memory and EEPROM unprotection key, and in-application programming status registers. After another reserved range, it gives DMA1 global configuration and interrupt registers and channel 0 configuration, status/priority, transfer-count, peripheral-address, and memory-address registers, including reset values and reserved addresses.
sections.short_description: Begins the general hardware register map with reserved address space, flash programming registers, and DMA1 global and channel 0 registers.

sections.title: DMA1 channels 1–3 register map
sections.summary: This continuation lists DMA1 channel 1 and channel 2 configuration, status/priority, transfer-count, peripheral-address, and memory-address registers, along with intervening reserved addresses. It then starts channel 3’s configuration, status/priority, transfer-count, and peripheral address registers. The entries identify channel-specific register labels, address fields, and reset states.
sections.short_description: Continues the general register map with DMA1 channel 1, 2, and 3 register addresses and reset values.

sections.title: DMA, system configuration, interrupts, power, and clock registers
sections.summary: The register map completes DMA1 channel 3 memory-address registers and lists reserved space. It then covers system configuration remapping registers; external interrupt control, status, and port selection; WFE control registers; reset control and status; power control/status; and the first clock control and peripheral clock-gating registers. Register addresses and reset values are provided where shown.
sections.short_description: Completes DMA1 channel 3 entries and maps system configuration, interrupt, reset, power, and initial clock registers.

sections.title: Clock, watchdog, BEEP, and RTC registers
sections.summary: The map continues with clock peripheral gating, configurable clock, external clock, system clock switching and status, clock security, BEEP clock, HSI calibration, and regulator registers. It then lists window and independent watchdog registers with reserved ranges, followed by BEEP control/status registers and the RTC time registers RTC_TR1–RTC_TR3. Reset states and reserved regions are included as shown.
sections.short_description: Continues the hardware register map through clock controls, watchdogs, BEEP, and the first RTC time registers.

sections.title: RTC date and control registers
sections.summary: The section continues the STM8L050J3 hardware register map, detailing RTC date, control, and related registers; SPI1, I2C1, and USART1 registers; and TIM2, TIM3, and TIM4 registers. It also covers the infrared control register and ADC1 configuration, status, data, threshold, channel-sequence, and trigger-disable registers. Register addresses, descriptions, reset values, and reserved areas are identified.
sections.short_description: Catalogs RTC, communication, timer, infrared, and ADC1 registers, including their addresses, reset values, and reserved areas.

sections.title: Reserved area, RI, and comparator registers
sections.summary: The map notes reserved areas before listing RI timer input-capture routing, I/O input, control-mode, switch, group-control, analog-switch, and resistor-control registers. It also gives the COMP1/COMP2 comparator control and status registers, their addresses, and reset values. The section resumes with RI I/O control and mask registers, ending at RI_IOSR4.
sections.short_description: Covers a reserved address gap and the RI input-routing, I/O control, switch, analog-switch, resistor-control, and comparator registers.

sections.title: CPU, interrupt controller, SWIM, and debug registers
sections.summary: This section finishes the RI register map and notes that specified registers are reset at power-on rather than by system reset. It then catalogs CPU registers, including accumulator, program counter, index registers, stack pointer, and condition code register; global configuration and interrupt software-priority registers; and SWIM and debug-module registers. The continued table lists additional debug control/status and enable-function registers, with notes on reserved addresses and debug-module-only access.
sections.short_description: Lists CPU register addresses and reset states, interrupt software-priority registers, SWIM and debug-module registers, plus access and reserved-area notes.

sections.title: Interrupt vector mapping: reset through ADC1
sections.summary: The interrupt vector mapping table describes interrupt numbers, source blocks, event descriptions, wakeup behavior in Active-halt and wait modes, and vector addresses. Entries run from reset and software trap through TLI, FLASH, DMA1, RTC, PVD, external interrupts, clock, and ADC1. The table also indicates which sources can wake the device in the listed modes; ADC1 covers end-of-conversion, analog-watchdog, and overrun events.
sections.short_description: Introduces the interrupt mapping table and gives vector addresses, sources, descriptions, and wakeup behavior for reset, system and peripheral interrupts through ADC1.

sections.title: Interrupt vector mapping continued: TIM2
sections.summary: The continued table repeats the interrupt-mapping column headings and begins the TIM2 entries. IRQ 19 covers update, overflow, trigger, and break interrupts at vector 0x00 8054; IRQ 20 covers TIM2 capture/compare at 0x00 8058. Both entries show no wakeup in Active-halt and wakeup support in the listed wait modes.
sections.short_description: Continues the interrupt mapping table with TIM2 update, overflow, trigger, break, and capture/compare interrupts and their vector addresses and wakeup behavior.

sections.title: Device interrupt and wake-up notes, option-byte configuration, and key electrical limits and operating conditions.
sections.summary: The excerpt lists interrupt vectors and wake-up behavior, then describes STM8L050J3 option bytes for readout protection, user boot-code sizing, watchdog behavior, oscillator startup delays, brownout reset, and bootloader selection. It also introduces electrical-parameter measurement conditions and summarizes absolute limits and operating ranges, including supply voltage, temperature, current, injection, and reset-threshold characteristics.
sections.short_description: Device interrupt and wake-up notes, option-byte configuration, and key electrical limits and operating conditions.

sections.title: Voltage-monitor thresholds and MCU current consumption across operating modes and conditions.
sections.summary: This section of the STM8L050J3 datasheet gives POR/BOR and programmable voltage detector (PVD) thresholds, then describes supply-current characteristics. It provides typical and maximum current figures for Run and Wait modes across clock sources, CPU frequencies, code execution from RAM or Flash, and temperature conditions, plus plots of current versus supply voltage. It also begins the Low-power run mode current specifications. Measurement conditions, design and characterization guarantees, and notes on oscillator and Flash-related current are included.
sections.short_description: Voltage-monitor thresholds and MCU current consumption across operating modes and conditions.

sections.title: Power-consumption figures and external-clock electrical specifications for the STM8L050J3.
sections.summary: The section gives STM8L050J3 electrical characteristics, including current consumption in Low-power wait, Active-halt, and Halt modes across supply voltages and temperatures. It notes how enabled peripherals, TIM2 operation, oscillator configuration, and external-crystal LSE current affect measurements. It also lists peripheral current draw, current under external reset, and HSE/LSE external-clock input frequency, voltage, capacitance, and leakage specifications.
sections.short_description: Power-consumption figures and external-clock electrical specifications for the STM8L050J3.

sections.title: Clock-source specifications and selected memory and I/O electrical characteristics for the STM8L050J3.
sections.summary: The section specifies STM8L050J3 clock-source, memory, and I/O electrical characteristics. External HSE oscillators support 1–16 MHz and external LSE oscillators run at 32.768 kHz; both require nearby load capacitors, with typical startup times of 1 ms and 1 s respectively. Internal HSI is nominally 16 MHz, with factory-calibrated accuracy and user trimming, while LSI spans 26–56 kHz with a typical wake-up time of 200 µs. The section also summarizes RAM and nonvolatile-memory operating limits and endurance, I/O injection robustness, and GPIO input thresholds, leakage, pull-up resistance, and capacitance.
sections.short_description: Clock-source specifications and selected memory and I/O electrical characteristics for the STM8L050J3.

sections.title: GPIO output driving characteristics
sections.summary: Presents output-low and output-high voltage specifications for high-sink and true open-drain I/O, including the PA0 high-sink LED driver. It notes that sourced and sunk currents must stay within absolute maximum ratings and aggregate supply-current limits. Figures show typical VOL and VOH behavior at 3.0 V and 1.8 V.
sections.short_description: This section covers output voltage limits and typical voltage-versus-current characteristics for high-sink, true open-drain, and PA0 LED-driver pins.

sections.title: SPI1 serial peripheral interface
sections.summary: Defines SPI1 clock frequency and timing characteristics under the stated operating conditions, with references to alternate-function I/O characteristics. The table includes NSS setup and hold, SCK high and low periods, data input setup and hold, and output access, disable, valid, and hold times. Timing diagrams illustrate slave operation for CPHA=0 and CPHA=1 and master operation; measurement points use CMOS levels of 0.3 VDD and 0.7 VDD. Footnotes identify values based on design simulation or characterization and explain timing interpretations.
sections.short_description: This section covers SPI1 electrical characteristics and timing in slave and master modes, including setup, hold, access, and output timing.

sections.title: I2C interface characteristics
sections.summary: Lists I2C1 timing characteristics for Standard mode and Fast mode, including SCL low and high periods, SDA setup and hold, bus rise and fall times, START and repeated-START timing, STOP timing, and bus-free time. The stated capacitive-load condition notes that an 8 MHz clock is needed to achieve the maximum Fast-mode rate of 400 kHz. Protocol-based values are not production-tested. Notes describe expected speed tolerance and dependence on external components; the accompanying application diagram shows pull-ups and timing measurement points.
sections.short_description: This section covers Standard-mode and Fast-mode I2C timing limits, operating notes, and a typical bus application diagram.

sections.title: Embedded reference voltage
sections.summary: Specifies the internal reference voltage consumption and output voltage, output load, startup times for the reference and its buffer, and reference accuracy and stability over temperature and time. The table notes characterization-based values and includes conditions and footnotes for guaranteed or production-tested parameters. Additional entries give ADC sampling time when reading the internal reference and the consumption of the internal-reference buffer used by the ADC.
sections.short_description: This section covers internal reference-voltage electrical characteristics, startup, buffer behavior, accuracy, temperature stability, and ADC sampling and consumption.

sections.title: Comparator characteristics
sections.summary: Comparator specifications are provided for the STM8L050J3, with values guaranteed by design or characterization unless noted. Comparator 1 operates across the stated analog-supply and temperature ranges; its input range, internal reference voltage, timing, offset, and consumption are tabulated. Comparator 2 specifications distinguish fast and slow modes, with propagation delay and consumption dependent on supply voltage and operating mode. Notes describe characterization and production test conditions, including the input step and overdrive used for delay measurements, and clarify that comparator current excludes the internal reference.
sections.short_description: This section presents comparator 1 and comparator 2 electrical characteristics, including operating ranges, startup and propagation delays, offset error, and current consumption.

sections.title: 12-bit ADC1 characteristics
sections.summary: ADC1 characteristics include analog and reference supply ranges, reference-pin current, conversion voltage range, temperature range, external input resistance, sample-and-hold capacitance, sampling-clock limits, conversion rate, trigger frequency and latency, and sampling and conversion times. The continued table gives wakeup and inter-conversion timing and refers to the internal-reference startup time. Notes explain that VREF current includes constant and sampling-related components, giving peak and average consumption estimates, and state that VREF− or VSSA must be grounded. The following accuracy tables are identified as characterization-based rather than production-tested.
sections.short_description: This section specifies ADC1 supply, reference, input, timing, and current characteristics, along with conversion timing notes and accuracy-test context.

sections.title: ADC1 accuracy and input design guidance
sections.summary: ADC1 accuracy tables list differential and integral nonlinearity, total unadjusted error, offset, and gain error under different supply and sampling-clock conditions. Figures illustrate ADC accuracy, the sample-and-hold input model, and dynamic current drawn from VREF+ during conversion. The input-model guidance notes that PCB and pad parasitic capacitance can reduce accuracy and recommends lowering the ADC clock when parasitic capacitance is high. A table specifies maximum external input resistance for a 16 MHz ADC clock across sampling durations and supply ranges; some short-sampling conditions are not allowed. The section then introduces general PCB design guidance, recommending close placement of good-quality ceramic decoupling capacitors.
sections.short_description: This section covers ADC accuracy results, input-model figures, reference-pin current during conversion, and maximum source resistance for sampling times.

sections.title: Decoupling and EMC characteristics
sections.summary: This section presents the supply and reference decoupling arrangement, EMC testing guidance and susceptibility data, then concludes with SO8N package dimensions, marking, recommended footprint, and thermal characteristics.
sections.short_description: Supply and reference decoupling, EMC test guidance and data, and SO8N package and thermal specifications.

sections.title: Ordering Information, Revision History, and Notice
sections.summary: Explains the STM8L050J3 ordering-code structure and directs readers to ST sales for available options. Lists document revisions from the initial 2017 release through revision 7 in 2022, followed by the manufacturer’s important notice, warranty and liability terms, trademark information, and document-use disclaimer.
sections.short_description: Ordering-code interpretation, document revision history, and legal notice.
